name: Upssets
tagline: A small paid web tool in the digital asset space; the exact feature set could not be pinned down at drafting time.

pricing.notes: AI-drafted from a site submission; price unverified.

verdictSummary: This one goes on the board with a caveat: we could not confirm the feature set, so the judgment is about the category rather than the specific product. Tools that organize, tag and batch-process your own files are close to a solved problem for a coding agent, and a local version usually beats the hosted one for speed and privacy. What does not survive a one-shot build is anything the product actually licenses or curates on your behalf, because that is content, not code. Until the details are verified, read the verdict as: the plumbing is a weekend, the library is not. Treat this page as provisional.
coreLoopDIY: A local web app that ingests files into a tagged, searchable library, groups them into named sets, and batch exports or converts them.
requirements: local disk space for the files
sharp or ffmpeg installed for thumbnails and conversions
whatYouLose: Any curated or licensed content the paid product ships with, which no prompt can conjure legally
A shareable hosted URL, so collaborators get a zip instead of a link
Mobile access unless you expose your machine to the network yourself
Ongoing maintenance: format quirks and codec updates become your problem
Whatever polish the paid UI has that you will not bother rebuilding
moatNotes: If the product's value is files it has rights to distribute, that is the whole moat and code is irrelevant. If it is just organization and processing, there is barely a moat at all.
whyPeopleStillPay: Because a hosted tool works from any device, in a browser, with no install step and no dependency hell, and because paying a small monthly fee is cheaper than an evening of debugging image pipelines. If the product bundles assets, people also pay for the license and the not having to hunt, which is a real service even when the software around it is thin.
notes: Filed at low confidence: the name reads like an asset tool and the public copy did not settle it, so the prompt targets the most likely shape.
prompt:
Build a local-first asset library and batch processor. Single user, runs on my machine, no accounts, no cloud, no telemetry.

Stack, no substitutions:
- Next.js (App Router) with TypeScript and Tailwind
- SQLite via better-sqlite3 for metadata
- Files stored on local disk under ./library, never in the database
- sharp for image thumbnails and conversion
- ffmpeg via child_process for video and audio thumbnails, degrade gracefully if the binary is missing

Features, in scope:
1. Drag-and-drop upload of many files at once. Compute a sha256 hash per file and skip exact duplicates.
2. On ingest, extract width, height, duration, mime type, byte size, and store them. Generate a thumbnail into ./library/.thumbs.
3. Grid browser with virtualized scrolling, thumbnail previews, and a detail drawer showing metadata.
4. Tags: free-form, many per asset, autocomplete on existing tags, bulk tag and untag on multi-select.
5. Sets: named collections, an asset can live in several, drag assets into a set, reorder within a set.
6. Search and filter: text match on filename and tags, plus filters for type, tag, set, and size range. Everything in one query string so URLs are shareable locally.
7. Batch actions on a selection: convert images to webp/png/jpg at a chosen max dimension, rename by pattern, export as a zip.
8. A single CLI script, npm run scan, that re-indexes ./library from disk so I can drop files in manually.

Out of scope: auth, multi-user, payments, any marketplace or store, stock content, cloud storage, sharing links, mobile app.

Config in .env: LIBRARY_PATH, THUMB_SIZE, MAX_UPLOAD_MB. Provide .env.example, never commit secrets.

Deliver a README with setup in under five commands, a seed script that generates a few dummy assets, and one integration test covering ingest, dedupe, tag, and zip export. Keep the UI plain and fast, dark theme, keyboard shortcuts for select-all and delete.
